03 – Are the mutants what we think they are?

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source

Bio253 HS2026 · validating stk1::Tn and stp1::Tn

Goal: before you interpret any “stk vs anc” or “stp vs anc” difference, check that the mutant strains really lack the protein they are supposed to lack – and only that one. This is routine in every good proteomics project.

The two mutants come from the Nebraska Transposon Mutant Library (NTML): a transposon (Tn) inserted into stk1 (kinase, also called pknB) or stp1 (phosphatase). In the genome, stp1 lies directly upstream of stk1.

Code 
source("../R/setup.R")
abundances <- read_abundances("total")
dea <- read_dea("total")

1. Find Stk1 and Stp1

Code 
KEY_PROTEINS |> filter(short_name %in% c("Stk1", "Stp1"))
short_name locus_tag protein_id role
Stp1 B7H15_06350 ARG45702.1 Ser/Thr phosphatase (mutated in ‘stp’)
Stk1 B7H15_06355 ARG45703.1 Ser/Thr kinase PknB (mutated in ‘stk’), downstream of stp1
Code 
find_protein(c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355")) |>
  select(locus_tag, product, protein_id, location, staa8_uniprot)
locus_tag product protein_id location staa8_uniprot
B7H15_06350 protein phosphatase ARG45702.1 1232295..1233038 Q2FZ65
B7H15_06355 serine/threonine protein kinase ARG45703.1 1233035..1235029 Q2FZ64

Question: look at the location column. Which gene comes first? Do they overlap?

plot_protein(c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355"), abundances)

  select(protein, sample, normalized_abundance) |>

Questions

  1. Is Stk1 gone in stk? Is it gone in every stk sample? (Look closely at each replicate.)
  2. What happens to Stk1 in the stp strain? Was that in your prediction?
  3. Is Stp1 gone in stp? How consistent are the replicates? Are some values as high as in the wild type? What could explain that (think: sample mix-up, carry-over, revertants, mixed culture, peptide mis-assignment)?
  4. Is Stp1 changed in stk?

4. The DEA view – and why it can mislead here

Code 
dea |>
  filter(locus_tag %in% c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355"),
         str_detect(contrast, "^(stk|stp)_vs_anc_at_")) |>
  mutate(protein = if_else(locus_tag == "B7H15_06350", "Stp1", "Stk1")) |>
  transmute(protein, contrast, diff = round(diff, 2), FDR = signif(FDR, 2), estimate_type) |>
  arrange(protein, contrast)
protein contrast diff FDR estimate_type
Stk1 stk_vs_anc_at_SN -2.83 5.3e-05 lod_imputed
Stk1 stk_vs_anc_at_SNpulse -1.66 2.6e-03 lod_imputed
Stk1 stk_vs_anc_at_TSB -2.34 2.4e-04 lod_imputed
Stk1 stp_vs_anc_at_SN -2.83 6.7e-05 lod_imputed
Stk1 stp_vs_anc_at_SNpulse -2.01 2.2e-04 lod_imputed
Stk1 stp_vs_anc_at_TSB -2.34 4.7e-05 lod_imputed
Stp1 stk_vs_anc_at_SN -0.17 8.3e-01 observed
Stp1 stk_vs_anc_at_SNpulse -0.40 5.6e-01 observed
Stp1 stk_vs_anc_at_TSB -0.17 8.4e-01 observed
Stp1 stp_vs_anc_at_SN -1.63 1.7e-01 observed
Stp1 stp_vs_anc_at_SNpulse -3.07 9.9e-03 observed
Stp1 stp_vs_anc_at_TSB -4.98 2.3e-02 observed

Question: Several rows are lod_imputed. What does a log2FC of, say, −5 mean when one group was never measured? Why might the FDR of the “absent” protein be less impressive than you expect?

5. A polar effect? Look at the neighbours

Transposon insertions can disturb the expression of genes downstream in the same operon (polar effect). If stp1::Tn reduces Stk1, the neighbourhood should tell us more.

Code 
neighbours <- sprintf("B7H15_%05d", seq(6335, 6370, by = 5))
read_annotation() |>
  filter(locus_tag %in% neighbours) |>
  select(locus_tag, product, location)
locus_tag product location
B7H15_06335 methionyl-tRNA formyltransferase 1228952..1229887
B7H15_06340 16S rRNA (cytosine(967)-C(5))-methyltransferase 1229884..1231191
B7H15_06345 23S rRNA (adenine(2503)-C(2))-methyltransferase RlmN 1231194..1232288
B7H15_06350 protein phosphatase 1232295..1233038
B7H15_06355 serine/threonine protein kinase 1233035..1235029
B7H15_06360 ribosome small subunit-dependent GTPase A 1235257..1236132
B7H15_06365 ribulose-phosphate 3-epimerase 1236133..1236777
B7H15_06370 thiamine pyrophosphokinase 1236784..1237425
Code 
plot_protein(neighbours, abundances)

Questions

  • Which neighbours are unaffected in stp? Which are affected?
  • Is “polar effect of the Tn insertion” the only explanation for low Stk1 in stp? (Alternatives: Stk1 protein unstable without Stp1, autoregulation, a second mutation in the strain …)
  • What would you check in the lab? (e.g. PCR / sequencing of the insertion site, RT-qPCR of stk1, complementation strain)
  • Consequence: if stp lacks both Stp1 and (mostly) Stk1, how should you interpret any stp_vs_anc result in the other notebooks?

6. Phospho sites on Stk1 and Stp1

Stk1 phosphorylates itself (autophosphorylation in its activation loop). If Stk1 is absent, its phospho-sites should be absent, too.

Code 
sites <- read_sites("STYH")
stk_stp_sites <- sites |>
  filter(locus_tag %in% c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355"))

stk_stp_sites |>
  group_by(locus_tag, site_id, residue, position, best_loc_prob, group) |>
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(intensity)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(site = paste0(residue, position)) |>
  select(locus_tag, site, best_loc_prob, any_of(GROUPS)) |>
  arrange(locus_tag, as.integer(str_extract(site, "[0-9]+")))
locus_tag site best_loc_prob anc_TSB anc_SNpulse anc_SN stk_TSB stk_SNpulse stk_SN stp_TSB stp_SNpulse stp_SN
B7H15_06355 S159 0.6208 3 2 2 0 0 0 1 0 0
B7H15_06355 T161 0.9215 2 3 3 0 0 0 0 0 0
B7H15_06355 S162 0.8911 3 3 3 0 0 0 0 0 0
B7H15_06355 T164 0.9370 3 3 3 0 0 0 3 1 2
B7H15_06355 T166 0.9362 3 3 3 0 0 0 3 1 1
B7H15_06355 H168 0.9028 3 3 3 0 0 0 1 2 2
B7H15_06355 T172 0.8654 3 3 2 0 0 0 0 2 1
B7H15_06355 Y175 0.5931 0 0 1 0 0 0 0 0 1
B7H15_06355 T231 0.8818 2 0 1 0 2 1 2 1 1
B7H15_06355 S240 0.8833 2 0 1 0 2 1 2 1 0
B7H15_06355 S242 0.8833 2 0 1 0 2 1 2 1 0
B7H15_06355 T288 1.0000 3 1 3 0 0 0 0 0 0
B7H15_06355 T314 0.9096 1 0 3 0 0 0 0 0 0
B7H15_06355 T315 0.8866 0 0 1 0 0 0 0 0 0

Numbers = in how many of the 3 replicates the site was detected.

Code 
plot_sites(unique(stk_stp_sites$site_id), sites)

Questions

  • Which Stk1 residues are phosphorylated in the wild type? Where are they in the protein (look up the kinase domain / activation loop of PknB, UniProt Q2FZ64 is the NCTC8325 ortholog)?
  • Are any Stk1 phospho-sites detected in the stk strain? If yes – where in the protein are they, and what could that say about where the transposon sits (a truncated protein?) or about the sample?
  • Are there phospho-sites on Stp1 at all?
  • One site is on a histidine. Keep it in mind for notebook 05.

title: "03 – Are the mutants what we think they are?"
subtitle: "Bio253 HS2026 · validating stk1::Tn and stp1::Tn"
---

**Goal:** before you interpret any "stk vs anc" or "stp vs anc" difference, check
that the mutant strains really lack the protein they are supposed to lack – and
*only* that one. This is routine in every good proteomics project.

The two mutants come from the Nebraska Transposon Mutant Library (NTML):
a transposon (Tn) inserted into *stk1* (kinase, also called *pknB*) or *stp1*
(phosphatase). In the genome, *stp1* lies directly upstream of *stk1*.

```{r setup}
source("../R/setup.R")
abundances <- read_abundances("total")
dea <- read_dea("total")
```

## 1. Find Stk1 and Stp1

```{r find}
KEY_PROTEINS |> filter(short_name %in% c("Stk1", "Stp1"))
find_protein(c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355")) |>
  select(locus_tag, product, protein_id, location, staa8_uniprot)
```

**Question:** look at the `location` column. Which gene comes first? Do they overlap?

## 2. Prediction

Write down **before** plotting:

| strain | Stp1 expected | Stk1 expected |
|---|---|---|
| anc | present | present |
| stk | ? | ? |
| stp | ? | ? |

## 3. Per-sample abundances

```{r plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
plot_protein(c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355"), abundances)
```

```{r table}
abundances |>
  filter(locus_tag %in% c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355")) |>
  mutate(protein = if_else(locus_tag == "B7H15_06350", "Stp1", "Stk1")) |>
  select(protein, sample, normalized_abundance) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = protein, values_from = normalized_abundance) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(v) round(v, 1)))
```

**Questions**

1. Is Stk1 gone in `stk`? Is it gone in *every* `stk` sample? (Look closely at
   each replicate.)
2. What happens to **Stk1 in the `stp` strain**? Was that in your prediction?
3. Is Stp1 gone in `stp`? How consistent are the replicates? Are some values as
   high as in the wild type? What could explain that (think: sample mix-up,
   carry-over, revertants, mixed culture, peptide mis-assignment)?
4. Is Stp1 changed in `stk`?

## 4. The DEA view – and why it can mislead here

```{r dea}
dea |>
  filter(locus_tag %in% c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355"),
         str_detect(contrast, "^(stk|stp)_vs_anc_at_")) |>
  mutate(protein = if_else(locus_tag == "B7H15_06350", "Stp1", "Stk1")) |>
  transmute(protein, contrast, diff = round(diff, 2), FDR = signif(FDR, 2), estimate_type) |>
  arrange(protein, contrast)
```

**Question:** Several rows are `lod_imputed`. What does a log2FC of, say, −5 mean
when one group was *never measured*? Why might the FDR of the "absent" protein be
less impressive than you expect?

## 5. A polar effect? Look at the neighbours

Transposon insertions can disturb the expression of genes **downstream in the
same operon** (polar effect). If *stp1::Tn* reduces Stk1, the neighbourhood
should tell us more.

```{r neighbours, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
neighbours <- sprintf("B7H15_%05d", seq(6335, 6370, by = 5))
read_annotation() |>
  filter(locus_tag %in% neighbours) |>
  select(locus_tag, product, location)

plot_protein(neighbours, abundances)
```

**Questions**

* Which neighbours are unaffected in `stp`? Which are affected?
* Is "polar effect of the Tn insertion" the only explanation for low Stk1 in
  `stp`? (Alternatives: Stk1 protein unstable without Stp1, autoregulation,
  a second mutation in the strain …)
* What would you check in the lab? (e.g. PCR / sequencing of the insertion site,
  RT-qPCR of *stk1*, complementation strain)
* **Consequence:** if `stp` lacks *both* Stp1 and (mostly) Stk1, how should you
  interpret any `stp_vs_anc` result in the other notebooks?

## 6. Phospho sites on Stk1 and Stp1

Stk1 phosphorylates itself (autophosphorylation in its activation loop). If Stk1
is absent, its phospho-sites should be absent, too.

```{r sites}
sites <- read_sites("STYH")
stk_stp_sites <- sites |>
  filter(locus_tag %in% c("B7H15_06350", "B7H15_06355"))

stk_stp_sites |>
  group_by(locus_tag, site_id, residue, position, best_loc_prob, group) |>
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(intensity)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(site = paste0(residue, position)) |>
  select(locus_tag, site, best_loc_prob, any_of(GROUPS)) |>
  arrange(locus_tag, as.integer(str_extract(site, "[0-9]+")))
```

Numbers = in how many of the 3 replicates the site was detected.

```{r plot-sites, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
plot_sites(unique(stk_stp_sites$site_id), sites)
```

**Questions**

* Which Stk1 residues are phosphorylated in the wild type? Where are they in the
  protein (look up the kinase domain / activation loop of PknB, UniProt Q2FZ64
  is the NCTC8325 ortholog)?
* Are any Stk1 phospho-sites detected in the `stk` strain? If yes – where in the
  protein are they, and what could that say about **where** the transposon sits
  (a truncated protein?) or about the sample?
* Are there phospho-sites on Stp1 at all?
* One site is on a histidine. Keep it in mind for notebook 05.
